cards.d: An attorney is one who gives others advice about the law.
cards.e: The attorney appeared in front of the judge for me.
cards.ielts: Free legal advice should be available to everyone, since people who cannot afford an attorney are at a serious disadvantage in court.

cards.d: When something is chronic, it happens over and over again over time.
cards.e: He had chronic pain in his chest and needed to see a doctor.
cards.ielts: A sedentary lifestyle increases the risk of chronic diseases such as diabetes and heart problems, placing pressure on healthcare systems.

cards.d: Discipline is training that helps people follow the rules.
cards.e: One of the teacher’s jobs is to teach her students discipline.
cards.ielts: Some teachers believe that strict discipline in schools produces better results, while others prefer to encourage independence and creativity.

cards.d: A donor is somebody who gives something to an organization.
cards.e: He was proud to be a blood donor.
cards.ielts: The new children’s hospital was built entirely with money from private donors, without any financial support from the government.

cards.d: A fellow is someone who shares a job or quality with someone else.
cards.e: All of my fellow patients at the hospital have also complained about the food.
cards.ielts: My fellow students and I organised a campaign to persuade the university to install more recycling bins on campus.

cards.d: Gossip is information that might be untrue but is still discussed anyway.
cards.e: The friends exchanged gossip about the people they knew in school.
cards.ielts: Social media has made it easier than ever for gossip about celebrities to spread around the world within a matter of minutes.

cards.d: To graduate from a school means to complete and pass all courses of study there.
cards.e: At the end of the spring, my friends and I will graduate from high school.
cards.ielts: The number of students who graduate from university each year has doubled, yet many still struggle to find suitable jobs.

cards.d: Graffiti is words or drawings in public places.
cards.e: The wall was covered with colorful graffiti.
cards.ielts: Some people regard graffiti as vandalism, whereas others see it as a form of street art that brightens up dull urban areas.

cards.d: A guardian is someone who protects somebody or something.
cards.e: The librarians are the guardians of the books.
cards.ielts: Teachers should not be seen as the only guardians of children’s education; parents must also take responsibility at home.

cards.d: To implicate someone is to show that they have done a crime or something bad.
cards.e: The man was implicated in the theft at the store.
cards.ielts: Several senior officials were implicated in the corruption scandal, which led to widespread protests against the government.

cards.d: Kin is a person’s family and relatives.
cards.e: His kin were all farmers.
cards.ielts: In traditional societies, elderly people are usually looked after by their kin rather than being placed in care homes.

cards.d: A referee is a person who makes sure that the rules are followed in sports.
cards.e: The soccer player didn’t agree with the referee.
cards.ielts: If I could have any job, I would like to be a football referee, because I love sport and enjoy making quick decisions.

cards.d: To sever something is to cut through it completely.
cards.e: He severed the string using scissors.
cards.ielts: During the storm, falling trees severed power lines, leaving thousands of households without electricity for several days.

cards.d: A shaft is a handle of a tool or weapon.
cards.e: The golf club had a long wooden shaft that he held in his hands.
cards.ielts: Archaeologists found a spear with a wooden shaft that had survived for thousands of years in the dry desert soil.

cards.d: To stab means to cut someone or something with a sharp object like a knife.
cards.e: He stabbed the fork into the potato and passed it to his daughter.
cards.ielts: Knife crime has risen in some cities, and the government has responded by tightening laws after several teenagers were stabbed.

cards.d: A stimulus is something that causes growth or activity.
cards.e: Having a lot of money is a stimulus for people to buy more things.
cards.ielts: Tax cuts for small businesses can act as a stimulus for economic growth and create new jobs in rural areas.

cards.d: A suspicion is a feeling that something is possible or true in a crime.
cards.e: The police had a suspicion that the driver had stolen the purse.
cards.ielts: Police arrested the cashier on suspicion of stealing from the company after large sums of money disappeared from the accounts.

cards.d: To terminate something means to stop or end it.
cards.e: The trip was terminated after the car broke down.
cards.ielts: The company terminated the contracts of hundreds of workers after replacing them with automated machines in its factories.

cards.d: A theme is the main subject of a book, movie, or painting.
cards.e: The students discussed the book’s theme in class.
cards.ielts: The central theme of the documentary was climate change and its impact on farming communities in developing countries.

cards.d: Tuition is the amount of money paid to go to a school.
cards.e: University tuitions have increased by fifty percent in the last five years.
cards.ielts: Some argue that university tuition should be free, as high fees prevent talented students from poorer families from studying.
